definitions.gloss: to sneak in, to steal into, to slip in secretly
definitions.explanation: To enter a place secretly and without being noticed, often with the intent to do something covert. Can refer to physical intrusion by a person or the gradual, unnoticed arrival of something abstract.

examples.japanese: ⟦{泥棒|どろぼう}→泥棒：01688_dorobou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{忍|しの}び{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: A thief snuck into the house.

examples.japanese: ⟦{猫|ねこ}→猫：02237_neko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いつの{間|ま}にか→いつの間にか：01812_itsunomanika⟧⟦{部屋|へや}→部屋：00507_heya⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{忍|しの}び{込|こ}んで⟦いた→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: A cat had slipped into the room without anyone noticing.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夜中|よなか}→夜中：01008_yonaka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦こっそり→こっそり：05890_kossori⟧⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{校舎|こうしゃ}→校舎：02801_kousha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{忍|しの}び{込|こ}んだこと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: I once snuck into the school building in the middle of the night.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound verb combining ⟦{忍|しの}ぶ→忍ぶ：16953_shinobu⟧ (to endure; to hide) and ⟦{込|こ}む→込む：00719_komu⟧ (to go in deeply). Emphasizes stealth and secrecy. Common in crime reporting, mystery fiction, and everyday stories about entering somewhere covertly.

COMMON PATTERNS:
Godan verb ending in む. Takes ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ to mark the destination: X⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{忍|しの}び{込|こ}む.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{忍|しの}び{込|こ}む: to sneak into a house
- ⟦{部屋|へや}→部屋：00507_heya⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{忍|しの}び{込|こ}む: to steal into a room
- ⟦こっそり→こっそり：05890_kossori⟧{忍|しの}び{込|こ}む: to sneak in secretly
- ⟦{夜中|よなか}→夜中：01008_yonaka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{忍|しの}び{込|こ}む: to sneak in at night
